findings.summary: Focus text with a newline would break the one-line status display
findings.evidence: set_focus trims the text but keeps inner newlines. `focus       {focus}` would then spread over several status lines. The commit subject already uses only the first line.

findings.summary: RealSteps::priority_caps quietly falls back to the defaults if the config cannot be read
findings.evidence: `.unwrap_or_default()` on a failed JobConfig::at gives 3/10 and logs nothing. This is harmless because the defaults equal the configured values, but a config error would not be reported.

summary: The change passes. It adds `athena focus`: a new `athena.focus/1` record stored at records/focus/focus-<n>.json. `athena focus` prints the latest focus, and `athena status` (text and JSON) shows it on a `focus` line. It also adds `[priority_caps]` to athena.toml (urgent 3, high 10, the same as the defaults in config.rs). When it plans, `athena plan` and drain now keep at most that many items at urgent and high. Extra items drop one tier in memory only, each with one `note demoted` line. Items a person gave a priority record are never demoted, and no record file is rewritten. I ran the new tests myself and all passed: the focus integration tests (5), the plan unit tests (31), the focus record tests, the caps config test and the drain prepare test. Athena's CI record shows fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed. All 8 criteria are met. The capping approach is sound: it reads the configured caps and the actual priority records instead of guessing, and judges the plan order against the capped tiers, so a demoted item is not reported as a priority contradiction. One file outside the deliverables list changed: xtask/shard-timings.txt gained one line, which an existing test requires for every new test target (minor). Two nits: focus text with a newline would spread the status line over several lines, and a config read failure falls back to the default caps without logging.
